subject: lemon-shaped planet
title: Webb Found a Planet Shaped Like a Lemon With an 8-Hour Year

scenes.text: Webb found a planet that isn't round. It's shaped like a lemon.
It's about as heavy as Jupiter, and one year there lasts less than eight hours.
Its sky holds soot clouds, and deep inside, carbon may squeeze into diamonds.
So what bent a giant planet out of shape?
It circles a dead star the size of a city, as heavy as our Sun, only a million miles away.
That star's gravity stretches the whole planet into a lemon. And slowly, it's eating it.

description:
NASA's Webb telescope studied PSR J2322-2650b, a Jupiter-mass planet stretched into a lemon shape by the pulsar it orbits every 7.8 hours, about a million miles away.
Its atmosphere is helium and molecular carbon with soot clouds, and carbon deep inside may form diamonds. It is a black widow system, where the pulsar slowly consumes its companion.
Would you rather see this planet or Saturn's rings up close?

first_comment: Of about 150 planets Webb has studied, none other has a carbon sky like this. What should Webb look at next?
